mainText:
Resources
Production planning
CNC prototypes and small-batch production
Validate the first sample

Define the sample checks before machining. Assembly fit and critical interfaces may be the main concerns; appearance or operation may also need approval. Record the acceptance criteria before releasing a repeat order.

Drawing questions
Use the sample to identify design questions related to fit, function or appearance.
Workholding and access
Review workholding and tool access while confirming the design.
Material, finish and acceptance
Check the specified grade, condition and final appearance. Define fit, function and sample acceptance checks. Confirm the prototype price and schedule for the specific part.
Prototype machining
Approve the repeat-order specification

For a repeat order, release one controlled drawing revision and carry the approved material and finish into the quotation. Agree the acceptance plan and the documents to accompany delivery.

Specification to carry forward
Agree revision approval and how changed features are identified.
Confirm material documents and the finish standard, including masking and dimensions after treatment.
Retain the approved specification unless a change is agreed.
Inspection records to agree
Define batch sampling and critical-feature records.
Confirm the measurement method, instrument evidence and available report format.
Agree the acceptance plan and delivery documents.

A drawing change may affect the approved sample. Confirm the changes before releasing the revised part.

Agree inspection records
Prepare the controlled drawing package
Plan the repeat order

Confirm the setup and machining sequence for the released revision, including critical datums, and whether the route changes with quantity. Request a new quote for the batch quantity and price, and confirm the production slot.

The economical batch size depends on the part and its setup.
Quantities are assessed for each drawing.

Minimum order
1 piece
Production lead time
7-14 business days

After drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional.

Share the part, quantity and required arrival date so we can quote price and delivery arrangements.

Low-volume production
Compare suppliers before committing

Compare the scope of each quote alongside its unit price.

Same specification

Make sure each quote uses the same drawing revision, material and finish.

Quoted scope

Check setup, inspection records, packaging and delivery basis are stated.

Exclusions or substitutions

Confirm that any exclusions or substitutions are clear.

Changes and repeat orders

Ask how changes, nonconforming parts and repeat orders will be handled.

Related part examples

The engine-cover example covers prototype clearances; the enclosure example covers thin walls and batch inspection.

Request a quote for the next batch

Send the approved drawing with quantities for the first order and expected repeat releases. Include the required arrival date and inspection records. The quotation confirms pricing and production timing, with finishing and shipping terms for that order.
